data.narrative:
Astroscale, a publicly listed Space & Aerospace company, is valued at $840M despite having raised $400M+ to date. The valuation sits within a peer universe of three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Rocket Lab ($40.0B), Planet Labs ($7.6B), and Firefly Aerospace ($2.9B).

Peer-median analysis constitutes the applicable triangulation method here. The median valuation across these three public Space & Aerospace peers is $7.6B, with a range spanning $2.9B to $40.0B. This wide dispersion reflects meaningful valuation heterogeneity within the sector, driven by differences in near-term revenue trajectory, launch cadence, and path to profitability. Public-comp anchoring via sector price-to-sales multiples (27.4x median across six public tickers including RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, and SATL) is not applicable due to the absence of disclosed revenue figures for the target.

The peer-median method implies a triangulated range of $6.4B (low) to $8.7B (high), with a midpoint of $7.6B. Astroscale's current $840M valuation sits substantially below this range, representing a 9.0x discount to the peer median. Key uncertainties include the sustainability of near-term contract wins, competitive positioning within launch services and on-orbit servicing, and execution risk on capital-intensive operational scaling. The single-method analysis limits confidence; additional revenue or EBITDA data would strengthen the valuation thesis.
